PullRequest.Title: agentHost: pace Agent Merge CI repair and reset the repair budget on progress
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #341960

## Problem

The logs from the issue show Agent Merge disabling itself with `repeatedAttempts=0, totalAttempts=7`: every repair turn addressed a *different* state, yet the per-enablement cap of 6 turns was hit 11 s after the turn that merged the fix from `main` and pushed. Three of those turns started 5–7 minutes apart while a workflow rerun the agent had requested was still queued, and one ended in an error while the machine was offline overnight.

## Changes

**Hold CI-only repair until the checks settle.** When failed CI is the only reason for a repair turn and checks are still pending, the turn starts once no check has changed for 10 minutes, or after 60 minutes at most. It never waits for every check to finish: some checks only complete after the others pass (for example, an approval check a team member satisfies once CI is green). Such a check never changes, so it reads as quiet. Turns that also address reviews or conflicts are never held, since they push and restart CI anyway. A held turn consumes no repair attempt. The controller re-evaluates exactly when the hold expires.

**Reset the repair budget on progress.** Each repair turn records the pull request head and its blockers as stable keys (`check:<name>`, `thread:<id>`, `feedback`, `conflicting`, `behind`). Before the next turn, a new head or any resolved blocker resets the repeated (3) and consecutive (6) limits. A failed check only counts as resolved once a check of that name passes, not merely because a new head has not reported it yet. A new lifetime limit of 20 turns per enablement, which progress never resets, bounds fix → new feedback → fix cycles.

**Accurate notices.** Running out of turns without progress and hitting the lifetime limit now have their own disable notices; "the same blockers remained" is only shown when that is the reason.

## Validation

- Added tests:
  - `Agent Merge repair pacing` suite in `agentMergeRerun.test.ts`: hold while checks change (including a check that never completes), maximum hold, combined repair not held, budget reset on a new head and on a resolved blocker, disable without progress and at the lifetime limit.
  - Pure tests for the progress and check-activity helpers in `agentMerge.test.ts`.
- Existing rerun tests that start with a sibling check in progress now wait out the quiet period first.
- **Tests were not run locally**: dependency installation failed against the npm feed with `E401` (expired credentials), so the worktree has no `node_modules`. I type-checked the changed source and test files with TypeScript 6.0.2: no errors in them; the only errors were in unrelated files and caused by the missing packages. Relying on CI for the test run.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed option, filter behavior, poll constants, pending predicate, snapshot observer, and Git subprocess call path are all explicit. Exact wall-clock cost varies by repository and pagination, but the 5x checks-request frequency and realistic optional-job trigger are deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub GraphQL requests and local git subprocesses
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For each Agent Merge pull request, cost repeats every minute for as long as any optional check remains queued or running; multiple enabled pull requests each have a separately coalesced resource stream.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excess GitHub API traffic plus increased agent-host CPU, filesystem I/O, and subprocess churn.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The subscription retained only required checks. Once the failed required check was completed, the shared checks fragment used its 5-minute backstop cadence; optional pending jobs could not accelerate it.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Setting includeOptional makes optional queued/running checks visible to PullRequestResourceService.checksPending, selecting checksPendingBackground (60 seconds) instead of checksBackstop (300 seconds), even after the required checks have settled.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `includeOptional: true` at line 1337 broadens the value consumed by the unchanged shared polling policy; `checksPending` treats every visible incomplete check as pending, so this changed option alone switches the cadence.
Findings.Title: Keep optional checks from forcing the pending poll cadence
Findings.Impact: A realistic long-running or stuck optional workflow causes five times as many checks refreshes (at least two GraphQL requests per refresh) while Agent Merge is enabled, and raises full controller/Git refresh frequency from the existing 2-minute mergeability cadence to about once per minute. This persists beyond the 10-minute CI hold and can last indefinitely until the optional job completes or Agent Merge is disabled.
Findings.Evidence: PullRequestResourceService uses a 60-second background interval when `checksPending(snapshot.checks.value)` is true and a 300-second backstop otherwise. The query fetches all checks and filters optional checks only before publishing, so this option changes the scheduler-visible state. Each checks fetch performs the rollup GraphQL query and, because `required: true`, the expected-suite GraphQL query (with pagination possible). Each published snapshot schedules AgentMergeController evaluation, whose critical path calls `attachSessionGitHubPullRequest`; that refresh computes session Git state through `git status`, `git remote`, `symbolic-ref`, divergence probes, and then calls `git branch --show-current`.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not expose optional pending state to the permanent shared polling predicate. Scope optional-check polling to an active CI-only hold, or make the resource cadence depend on required-check pending state while scheduling a bounded pacing-specific refresh for optional activity; return to the backstop cadence after the hold.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Before this change, a CI-only gate started a repair as soon as the prior turn completed whenever the fingerprint changed. The fingerprint includes failed check names/IDs, so normal CI fan-in can present successive distinct failure sets and bypass the unchanged-fingerprint backstop, producing one expensive agent repair turn per intermediate state.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Redundant agent repair turns and authoritative GitHub refreshes while workflows are still settling, consuming repair throughput and remote/local resources without waiting to collect the final failure set.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added CI hold computes a shared quiet/deadline window and returns before claiming a turn, coalescing changing pending-check states until ten minutes of quiet with a one-hour upper bound; non-CI repairs retain their immediate behavior.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: `evaluateAgentMerge` fingerprints actionable failed check IDs and context; `shouldRunFingerprint` permits every changed fingerprint immediately; `_completeTurn` authoritatively refreshes all subscribed fragments and immediately reevaluates. Thus successive check completions/failures could each start another full repair turn. Added line 1020 gates CI-only repair through `_getCIRepairHold`, and the pacing tests prove no prompt while checks change and one prompt after quiet. Blame identifies the original immediate budget/start path in the Agent Merge controller introduction.

Scenarios.Scenario: CI-only repair with a completed failed required check while required, optional, or not-yet-reporting suites are still pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A pull-request snapshot update schedules a debounced per-folder evaluation. Evaluation refreshes/validates local Git state, reads the shared snapshot, then either arms the quiet/deadline timer or dispatches the repair turn. GitHub polling is upstream of observing check activity; local Git validation and turn dispatch are on the repair critical path. Polls between state changes are otherwise background work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch check rollup and expected check suites from GitHub GraphQL, with pagination when needed
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least two requests per checks refresh because `required: true` loads expected suites; before the diff a settled required failure refreshed every 5 minutes, while after the diff any pending optional check refreshes every minute. One stream is shared per PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The boundary already existed, but optional checks were filtered before the scheduler's pending predicate, so they could not increase refresh frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provides activity observations for the quiet window; repeated unchanged polls are background work, but state publication drives repair evaluation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh session Git state using git status, remote, symbolic-ref and divergence probes, then validate the branch with git branch --show-current
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One multi-command Git refresh per debounced controller evaluation; the optional pending checks poll raises check-driven evaluations to about once per minute per PR, versus the existing roughly two-minute mergeability cadence and five-minute settled-check cadence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same validation ran per evaluation, but completed required checks did not cause optional pending jobs to publish checks snapshots every minute.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the evaluation can inspect the gate and release or continue the CI hold.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch an Agent Merge repair turn
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One turn after 10 minutes without observed check-state change, or after a 60-minute maximum hold; later repairs get a new bounded hold window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A distinct failed-check fingerprint could dispatch immediately after the previous turn, without coalescing CI fan-in.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the terminal expensive action being paced; the PR removes it from intermediate changing CI states.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One coalesced resource stream per pull request, multiplied by enabled Agent Merge pull requests. Check-query work also scales with paginated check contexts/suites; controller check digest work scales with the returned check/suite count. The realistic trigger is one long-running or stuck optional check alongside a completed required failure.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: PullRequestResourceService coalesces subscriptions for the same pull request and allows one checks-fragment operation per resource; initial independent fragments refresh in parallel through the shared request scheduler. Agent Merge evaluations are serialized per runtime key, while different enabled folders/PRs can evaluate independently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold subscription performs an authoritative core refresh followed by all interested fragments; adding optional checks does not add a new query shape because the rollup already fetches all contexts and previously filtered optional ones before publication. Warm behavior changes materially: an optional pending check now keeps the shared checks fragment on the 60-second pending cadence instead of the 300-second backstop. GraphQL responses are not negative-cached here; the resource itself is the coalescing/cache layer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added subscription option feeds the unchanged shared pending predicate, exact poll constants and query call path are explicit, and tests establish the pending optional-check trigger.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository size, query pagination, optional-workflow duration, and the number of concurrently enabled folders vary. The deterministic 60-second versus 300-second checks cadence and the multi-command Git evaluation path establish the mechanism; uncertainty affects severity, not causality.
Scenarios.Verdict: One medium performance regression was reported: optional checks permanently force pending-frequency checks polling and repeated full Git evaluations, even outside the bounded pacing need. The CI quiet-window itself fixes a concrete missing-coalescing regression and was recorded internally.

Scenarios.Scenario: Repair budget reset after a new head or a resolved blocker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After a candidate prompt survives CI pacing, the controller scans the already-loaded snapshot for head/blocker progress, computes counters, resolves the local repair baseline commit, dispatches the turn, and persists state. After turn completion it authoritatively refreshes the pull request before reevaluation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve and validate local Git state and repair baseline commit
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per candidate repair evaluation/turn, bounded by 20 turns per enablement; prior total budget bounded repeated repairs at six even after progress.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The boundary already existed; this PR permits more invocations only when prior turns demonstrably changed the head or resolved a blocker.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before a repair turn is claimed and again participates in post-turn safety checks.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authoritatively refresh core, conversation, checks, and mergeability after each completed repair turn
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped refresh per completed turn, with interested fragments fetched in parallel and individual collections paginated; lifetime cardinality can now reach 20 instead of the prior six total attempts when each turn makes progress.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same post-turn refresh existed, but the old total budget stopped after six turns regardless of demonstrated progress.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the controller evaluates whether another repair is needed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the next agent repair turn
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most 20 per enablement; repeated identical blockers still stop at three and no-progress sequences stop after six.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: At most six total prompts under the old counter, even when each turn advanced the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The turn is the intended user workflow, not speculative background work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Previous blocker keys are bounded by the prompt context caps; checks/reviews/comments scans scale with the snapshot collections. Repair turns are bounded to 20 per enablement, compared with the prior six-turn total cap when progress repeatedly occurred.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Progress computation is synchronous within a per-runtime serialized evaluation. A folder has at most one active repair turn; post-turn fragment refreshes run in parallel inside the resource service. Different folders can progress independently subject to shared request scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Progress uses the warm subscription snapshot and persisted controller state; no new network lookup or cache is introduced by the helper. A head change or resolved blocker resets only repeated/consecutive counters, while the persisted lifetime counter prevents unbounded retention or execution. Missing/new-head check results are deliberately not treated as a passed-check cache hit.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the increased bounded cardinality and progress checks; no evidence shows redundant work independent of the intended workflow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost and prevalence of long fix/new-feedback cycles are workload-dependent. The maximum is explicit and persisted, and useful progress is required before the old six-turn budget is reset.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The higher potential turn count is an explicit, bounded product tradeoff and only applies after demonstrated progress; repeated and lifetime safeguards prevent an unbounded burst or retention issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Repair that also addresses review feedback or merge conflicts while CI is pending
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Snapshot evaluation directly dispatches the combined repair after Git/target validation; it deliberately bypasses CI pacing because the repair is expected to push and restart CI.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate Git state and resolve repair baseline before dispatch
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per claimed combined repair turn, bounded by repair budgets.
Once per completed combined turn, grouped by pull request and fragment.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One combined action set per changed gate fingerprint, bounded by the repeated, no-progress, and lifetime counters. Review/blocker context is capped before prompt construction.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active turn per folder/chat ownership path, evaluations serialized per runtime key; shared pull-request fragment requests remain coalesced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses the existing warm pull-request snapshot and persisted fingerprint/counters. No optional-check hold timer or new cache is used for this branch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `ciOnlyRepair` is false for any mixed action set, so the new hold is not reached.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual review/conflict frequency varies, but neither boundary placement nor multiplicity is materially changed for this branch.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the existing immediate path and its bounded boundary calls are preserved.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. Reported one medium repeated-work/network regression from optional checks changing shared poll cadence, and recorded the CI quiet-window as a concrete fix for the original missing-coalescing Agent Merge controller behavior.
